elements.label: Figure O.3
elements.description:
Line chart titled "Poverty rates across different thresholds". Y-axis: "Poverty rate (%)", scale 0 to 25 in steps of 5. X-axis: years 2010 to 2020, one tick per year. Legend: General poverty rate (teal); GSO-WB poverty rate (grey); Multidimensional poverty rate (orange); World Bank LMIC poverty rate (yellow). No values are printed on the chart. Approximate readings:
- General poverty rate (teal): 2010 ~14, 2011 ~13, 2012 ~11, 2013 ~10, 2014 ~8, 2015 ~7, 2016 ~6; series ends in 2016.
- GSO-WB poverty rate (grey): 2010 ~21, 2012 ~17, 2014 ~13.5, 2016 ~10, 2018 ~7, 2020 ~5.
- Multidimensional poverty rate (orange): 2016 ~9, 2017 ~8, 2018 ~7, 2019 ~5.5, 2020 ~5.
- World Bank LMIC poverty rate (yellow): 2010 ~17, 2012 ~13, 2014 ~11, 2016 ~8, 2018 ~6.5, 2020 ~5.
All four series decline over the decade and converge near 5% by 2020.

Note printed below: "See Chapter 1 for definitions of the various lines." Source: GSO and World Bank.

elements.label: Figure O.4
elements.description:
Vertical bar chart titled "The number of poor, 2010–2020". Y-axis: "Number of poor (millions)", scale 0 to 15 in steps of 3. X-axis: years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: World Bank LMIC poor ($3.20/day 2011PPP), teal bars. No values are printed on the bars. Approximate readings: 2010 ~14.8, 2012 ~11.6, 2014 ~10.1, 2016 ~7.3, 2018 ~6.3, 2020 ~4.9 (millions). The number of poor falls steadily across the period, with the largest drop between 2010 and 2012.

Source printed below: "Source: World Bank staff calculations."
